Header:
Date: 2026-02-20
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Location: Zoom / recorded for Redwood marketing podcast
Attendees: Ariana Powell (Redwood AE), Dmitri Hsu (Redwood SE), Noah Lin (Redwood Marketing), Maya Chen (Brightwave Head of Product), Ethan Rivera (Brightwave CTO), Sophie Patel (Brightwave Marketing)
Links shared: draft episode link (private), Brightwave press kit (chat), internal benchmark doc (redacted)

Summary:
Informal podcast-style interview covering Brightwave's adoption of Redwood for production inference, cost/latency tradeoffs, and a success anecdote about a recent feature launch. Call recorded for marketing; consent confirmed.

Topics:
- Why Brightwave chose Redwood
- Migration from self-hosted model-serving to Redwood Dedicated
- Performance and cost wins; KV cache and batching notes
- Enterprise concerns: SSO, SOC 2, audit logs, VPC
- Customer quote and publishing next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Ariana: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — good to have the Brightwave crew here for the Redwood podcast. Quick audio check, you can say hi and where you're calling from?
[00:05] Maya: Hi, Maya here, calling from Boston — Head of Product at Brightwave.
[00:10] Ethan: Ethan, CTO, San Francisco. Slight echo on my end but OK.
[00:14] Sophie: Sophie, marketing, Boston as well — excited.
[00:18] Dmitri: Dmitri from Redwood, engineering — will pepper in with some technical bits.
[00:22] Noah: Noah, I run content at Redwood, I'll be helping with the edit.
[00:26] Ariana: Great, we'll cover the origin story, a couple of technical points, and then record a short quote at the end. Sound good?
[01:02] Ariana: Maya, how did Brightwave first learn about Redwood and what made you decide to partner?
[01:12] Maya: We were running models on k8s and as we scaled latency crept and costs spiked. We saw Redwood at a conference, did a quick demo with Ariana, ran a pilot and the results were convincing.
[01:38] Ethan: From infra we were worried about on-prem needs for some customers. Redwood Dedicated gave predictable throughput with managed ops. We did a three-week POC and saw solid results.
[01:57] Dmitri: I remember instrumenting the KV cache and sequence length distribution; tuning batching cut unit costs because your personalization workload is very spiky.
[02:15] Maya: That was huge. Cold starts on k8s caused timeouts; Dedicated stabilized latency.
[03:04] Ethan: p95 dropped from ~1.2s to ~420ms for the personalization route; cost per 1k tokens dropped ~40% after batching and caching suggestions. Numbers vary by workload.
[03:26] Sophie: For marketing that meant smoother UX for our in-app assistant and fewer support tickets after launch.
[04:16] Maya: Main concerns were SSO and auditability. We use Okta; Redwood's SAML and RBAC support plus audit log hooks into our SIEM were key. There was some back-and-forth but straightforward.
[04:44] Dmitri: We did a short security review — SOC 2 docs shared — and set up a private VPC peering for the Dedicated cluster to meet data-in-transit and residency concerns.
[05:20] Maya: Procurement/legal had clarifications on data retention; sorted within a week with the legal packet.
[06:12] Dmitri: Two low-effort high-impact optimizations: use a quantized model variant for small-token personalization calls, and enable prefix/KV caching for common prefixes; tuned batch window to 20–40ms.
[06:40] Ethan: The batch window mattered for tail latency; autoscale + batching needed iterations.
[07:36] Maya: Anecdote — during Black Friday our assistant's curated recommendations increased conversion on those flows by 12% and support deflection removed ~18 tickets/day at peak. Helped justify committed capacity.
[08:55] Ethan: We evaluated OpenAI endpoints, Anthropic, and smaller inference vendors (ModelServe Inc.). OpenAI was simple but higher cost at scale and fewer Dedicated/VPC options.
[10:16] Maya: We reassigned two infra engineers to ML pipelines after migration because model-serving ops load dropped.
[11:00] Dmitri: We provided knowledge transfer, playbooks for incident runbooks, and rollout procedures to support canary/A-B deployments.
[12:05] Sophie: For the site quote: 'Redwood made our LLM features reliable and cost-predictable, enabling us to ship personalization at scale.' Comfortable?
[12:24] Maya: Add 'with enterprise-grade controls' — full line: 'Redwood made our LLM features reliable and cost-predictable, enabling us to ship personalization at scale with enterprise-grade controls.'
[13:07] Ethan: Small hiccup: internal model alias vs Redwood catalog name caused a CI mapping issue caught in staging.
[14:10] Dmitri: When switching to quantized variants run a small eval suite; Brightwave's passed quickly.
[15:05] Sophie: Brightwave timeline — publish episode 2026-02-28; need edited cut by 2026-02-25 and assets earlier.
[16:10] Dmitri: We can share anonymized ranges for latency/cost improvements but will run those claims by legal.
[18:36] Rapid-fire:
[18:36] Ethan: Predictable capacity and easy peering.
[18:39] Maya: SE responsiveness and caching tips.
[18:42] Sophie: Marketing-friendly data to share.
[20:06] Maya (quote read for recording): 'Redwood made our LLM features reliable and cost-predictable, enabling us to ship personalization at scale with enterprise-grade controls.'
[21:15] Ariana: We'll follow up with assets and publish plan by email.
